COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 125 of 2026
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mrs. Sheetal Selwal, learned counsel for the 
revisionist.
2. There is a delay of 126 days in preferring the 
instant revision preferred by the revisionist for 
enhancement of maintenance granted by the Family 
Court.
3. Taking into consideration that the dispute is 
nothing but appears to be a matrimonial dispute, put 
up this matter on 25.02.2026.
4. By that time both the parties shall remain present 
in court.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist shall take 
steps to serve the respondent through all modes so that 
on the next date he shall remain present in court.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 23.02.2026

2. Notice on delay condonation application 
was issued to the respondent. As per office 
report, respondent has been served 
personally. Despite sufficient service, no one 
has put in appearance on behalf of 
respondent. 
3. Reasons furnished in the affidavit filed in 
support of delay condonation application are 
sufficient to condone the delay. Accordingly, 
the delay condonation application (I.A. No.1 of 
2026) is allowed and the delay in filing the 
revision is condoned. 
4. List on 23.07.2026.

Ms. Sheetal Selwal, learned counsel

2. Mr. Saurabh Kumar Pandey, learned 
counsel for respondent.
3. Parties are present in person before 
the Court. 
4. In the morning session, the matter 
was referred to mediation.
5. The mediation report has been 
received, wherein it is stated that there are 
chances of an amicable settlement. 
Accordingly, the matter has been fixed for 
further mediation on 04.11.2026.
6. In view of the above, list this case on 
04.11.2026.
7. The parties shall remain present 
before the Court on 04.11.2026 at 10:30 
A.M. for mediation.
8. Interim order, if any, continue till the 
next date of listing. 9. It is made clear that if any of the 
parties faces any difficulty in appearing on 
the next date fixed, they shall inform the 
other party in advance.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
